story: A regression tree predicts one constant value inside each leaf. Compare the supplied shallow and deep fits on the same sine samples, then inspect which sample values determine a selected leaf’s height.

aha.observation: At 90°, the target is 1, the depth-2 prediction is 0.734 and the depth-4 prediction is 0.933.

data.title: Compare both fits at the same angle.
data.heading: Same 25 rounded sine samples
data.prompt: how does a regression tree fit y = sin(x) with a step function at depth 2 versus depth 4?
data.instructions: Move the angle probe. Compare both leaf predictions at each supplied target.
calculations: Copy the supplied fitted edges and step heights, not uniform invented bins. The last repeated step entry closes the curve at 360°; it is not another leaf.
A leaf contains source sample angles between its adjacent midpoint edges; 360° belongs to the final leaf.
Mean = sum of supplied rounded integer targets / member count / 1000. Reference prediction = Math.round(integerSum/memberCount)/1000, using the reference rounding convention.
This preserves the source +0.130 and −0.129 for means +0.1295 and −0.1295; the 16-leaf peak mean is 0.9328 and displayed height 0.933.
Probe residual = supplied target − selected prediction. All targets, leaf means, sums and residuals use the supplied rounded data.
